title: Jubilant Light Indian Dough Gulab Jamun
description: Aerated and resinous Indian dish featuring szechuan peppercorns, long-fermentation-dough, and vegetarian-friendly ingredients, formed into gulab jamun and cooked in an iron teppan.
instructions: Combine flour, yeast, salt, and szechuan peppercorn powder in a large bowl to make the dough.
Gradually add milk to the dry ingredients and knead the dough for 10 minutes.
Let the dough ferment for 4 hours in a warm place.
Heat the iron teppan over medium heat and add vegetable oil.
Once the oil is hot, add the fermented dough to the teppan and cook for 5 minutes on each side.
Remove the dough from the teppan and soak it in gulab syrup for 30 minutes.
Serve the gulab jamun warm, garnished with rose water and cardamom powder if desired.
Repeat the process to make multiple gulab jamun.
Let the gulab jamun cool before storing them in an airtight container.
